hypotheses.text: Mild to moderate postnatal microcephaly (HP:0000252) is a recurrent phenotypic feature present in 20-25% of individuals with FBXO11-related disorder and is more frequent than macrocephaly (HP:0000256), refuting characterizations of head circumference being typically skewed toward normal-to-macrocephalic.
hypotheses.rationale: The initial prior stated that head circumference is typically normal to mildly macrocephalic with microcephaly being rare. Multiple systematic cohorts instead demonstrate that microcephaly is observed in approximately 20-25% of individuals and is consistently noted to be more common than macrocephaly.

evidence.text: In the initial cohort of 20 individuals, microcephaly was documented in 4 of 19 assessed individuals (21.1%) whereas macrocephaly was documented in only 2 of 19 (10.5%), with microcephaly occurring preferentially in individuals with likely gene-disrupting variants.

source.title: De novo variants in the F-box protein FBXO11 in 20 individuals with a variable neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: microcephaly (4/19) or macrocephaly (2/19)... microcephaly and obesity occurred more frequently in individuals with LGD variants

evidence.text: In an expanded international cohort of 21 previously unreported individuals, microcephaly occurred in 24% of cases, while macrocephaly was not identified as a recurrent feature.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Microcephaly occurred in 24%, while seizures were present in 43%.

evidence.text: Growth parameter analysis across 23 additional individuals showed that growth parameters are variable, with microcephaly and short stature being explicitly noted as more common than macrocephaly and tall stature.

source.title: De novo missense variants in FBXO11 alter its protein expression and subcellular localization
source.quote: Growth parameters are highly variable with short stature and microcephaly being more common than tall stature and macrocephaly.

evidence.text: A familial report of 3 affected individuals with a frameshift duplication in FBXO11 documented mild intellectual disability and macrocephaly in all 3 individuals.

source.title: The first familial case of inherited intellectual developmental disorder with dysmorphic facies and behavioral abnormalities (IDDFBA) with a novel FBXO11 variant
source.quote: All of our three affected individuals had mild ID and macrocephaly.

hypotheses.text: Major structural congenital malformations, specifically complex congenital heart defects (HP:0001627) and congenital limb-reduction deficiencies (HP:0002814), exhibit near-zero penetrance in FBXO11-related disorder, providing robust negative discrimination against disorders such as Cornelia de Lange syndrome or Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome.
hypotheses.rationale: While minor anomalies (such as cleft palate/uvula or minor digit anomalies) are observed, large visceral organ defects and limb-reduction deficiencies have not been reported in systemic cohort assessments, serving as high-confidence negative discriminators.

evidence.text: In 20 individuals, structural anomalies were limited to cleft lip/palate or bifid uvula (3/20) and minor skeletal anomalies, without complex cardiac malformations or limb-reduction deficiencies.

source.title: De novo variants in the F-box protein FBXO11 in 20 individuals with a variable neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: cleft lip or palate or bifid uvula (3/20), and minor skeletal anomalies.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 12 affected individuals from 5 families in China, major organ malformations were conspicuously absent in all affected individuals.

source.title: FBXO11 variants are associated with intellectual disability and variable clinical manifestation in Chinese affected individuals
source.quote: Distinguishingly, malformation was not observed in all the affected individuals.

hypotheses.text: Neurodevelopmental regression and progressive neurodegeneration (HP:0002376) do not occur in FBXO11-related disorder; the disease course is consistently static developmental delay rather than a progressive neurodegenerative process.
hypotheses.rationale: Differentiating FBXO11 from mitochondrial, lysosomal, or secondary neurodegenerative encephalopathies depends on proving that the cognitive and motor deficits represent failure/delay in achievement rather than loss of acquired milestones.

evidence.text: In 21 individuals described by Goel et al., brain imaging anomalies were nonspecific, without progressive cerebral or cerebellar atrophy, and core cognitive deficits presented as static intellectual disability.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Brain imaging abnormalities were nonspecific and did not consistently correlate with epilepsy.

new_directions.question_text: Does variant class (likely gene-disrupting/nonsense/frameshift versus missense) correlate specifically with microcephaly versus macrocephaly in FBXO11-related disorder?
new_directions.rationale: Gregor et al. (2018) suggested that microcephaly was enriched in individuals with likely gene-disrupting variants compared to missense variants, whereas Lee et al. (2020) observed macrocephaly in a frameshift duplication family. Clarifying this will determine whether cranial size variations reflect distinct molecular mechanisms.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence and spectrum of cleft palate, bifid uvula, and velopharyngeal insufficiency in FBXO11-related disorder across all published cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Cleft palate/bifid uvula is reported in 3/20 patients in Gregor et al. (2018) and could serve as an affirmative discriminator from other behavioral/ID conditions if penetrant at >10-15%.
